subject: POC Observability Plan & Next Steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura@fintechx.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: POC Observability Plan & Next Steps

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for a great discovery call this morning — really appreciate the clarity on your goals for the POC. Per our chat, I wanted to capture a proposed observability plan, success criteria, and clear next steps so we can kick off the trial on a firm footing. Below is a concise plan you can share with the Eng/DevOps team.

1) Goals & success criteria
- Latency: p95 end-to-end request latency < 350ms and p99 < 700ms for 95% of traffic during steady-state test windows.
- Availability: No more than 1 hour of degraded service for the POC window; critical fallback works (model variant fallback).
- Cost: Token cost per 1M tokens stays within the mutual action plan target (see attachment).
- Observability integration: Request traces and structured logs are ingested into FintechX APM/observability within 24 hours and dashboards reflect KV cache hit-rate and batching efficiency.
- Quality: Model output passes the agreed prompt-set regression checks (we'll run the baseline evaluation you provided).

2) What we'll deliver (Redwood)
- POC dashboard templates (Grafana/LookerStudio): latency (p50/p95/p99), error-rate, token consumption, cost, model variant split, KV cache hit-rate, batching metrics.
- Tracing hooks: distributed trace spans for request lifecycle, op latency breakdowns (tokenization, model inference, streaming), and sample trace links in the dashboard.
- Log export: structured request/response logs (masked per agreement) delivered to an S3 bucket or GCS + example BigQuery schema if you prefer.
- Alerting runbook: simple SLO alerts (p95 latency breach, error-rate spikes, cost threshold alerts).

3) What we need from FintechX
- Confirmation of desired S3/GCS bucket or a temporary role we can write to for the POC by Mar 13.
- Contact for APM integration (owner for distributed tracing) — is Jason the right person to own that?
- Short prompt-set and baseline evals (CSV) by Mar 12 so we can run quality checks during the POC.

4) Timeline (proposed)
- Mar 13: Access provided (bucket/roles) + shared Drive doc live.
- Mar 15: POC kickoff — Managed endpoint + instrumentation enabled.
- Mar 15–22: Warm-up & integration (dashboards live, traces arriving).
- Mar 23–27: Controlled load tests and prompt-set evaluation.
- Mar 29: POC review — telemetry + quality review, recommend next steps.

5) Ownership & contacts
- Redwood: Marissa Cole (commercial lead), Aditya Rao (Instrumentation & runtime support), Marcus Lin (Infra/config + dashboard templates).
- FintechX: Laura Chen (POC sponsor), Jason Lee (APM/observability owner) — please confirm/update.

6) Next actions (simple):
- Laura: confirm timeframe and provide bucket/role or preferred export path by EOD Mar 13.
- Jason: confirm tracing endpoint/collector and whether you want OTLP or Zipkin format.
- Marissa/Aditya/Marcus: we will create the Drive doc and share access once bucket details are confirmed.

Attachments: poc-observability-draft.pdf (short plan), mutual-action-plan.xlsx (timing/pricing).

If this looks good I’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff for Mar 15 and loop in the Eng leads.

Thanks —
Marissa

From: Laura Chen <laura@fintechx.com>

Cc: Jason Lee <jason.lee@fintechx.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 11:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: POC Observability Plan & Next Steps

Thanks Marissa — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A few quick items from our side:

- Timeline: Mar 15 kickoff works for us, and we can provide the bucket/role by end of day Mar 13.
- Tracing: Jason prefers OTLP; we'll confirm collector endpoint by EOD 3/12.
- Latency success criteria: the p95 < 350ms target is ambitious for our upstream network. Can we add a note that the latency SLO is "service-level" (end-to-end) and we'll evaluate both internal (FintechX network) and Redwood runtime components separately? If p95 is within 450ms for the first week we can iterate down.
- Data retention/compliance: We need a short confirmation that logs exported for the POC will be retained for 30 days and encrypted at rest. Is that the default?

Also, we've shared the baseline prompt-set (attached as CSV) with Jason and he will validate for the test windows.

If you can update the Drive doc with the OTLP format and the 30-day retention callout, we can mark this ready.

—Laura
Laura Chen
Head of Product, FintechX
laura@fintechx.com

Hi Laura,

Quick answers from the instrumentation side:
- Retention & encryption: For the POC we can support 30-day retention in the export bucket; all exports from our side are encrypted at rest using customer-managed keys if you provide KMS permissions, otherwise we use our managed encryption. We'll note the retention and encryption option in the Drive doc.
- Latency split: We agree it's helpful to separate "network + customer infra" vs "Redwood runtime". We'll instrument spans so you can see the outbound network hop vs inference time. In early tests, we'll capture both and annotate the dashboard so p95 can be shown as both end-to-end and runtime-only.
- OTLP: OTLP is fine. Please share the collector endpoint and auth method (API key or mTLS) and we'll configure the tracer.

I'll create the initial Grafana dashboard and push a link to the Drive doc by EOD Wed (links below). Marcus will publish the LookerStudio template as well.

Quick links:
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/fintechx/poc-observability (shared with your @fintechx.com domain)
- Jira: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/POC-342 (tracking infra/setup tasks)
